thread:
incident-bot: P1 ALERT: continuous-batcher service (us-east-1) reporting repeated OOM/killed-by-OOM kernel events on GPU nodes, sustained batch-queue growth, large latency spike. Dash: https://grafana.redwood/dbc/continuous-batcher | trace: trace-0a9f

Priya K: ACKing and joining. What metrics are worst? which pods/nodes?

incident-bot: Metrics snapshot: 95p latency jumped 120ms -> 3.2s in last 5m; error rate increased from 0.2% -> 18%; pod evictions: 7/12 pods restarted in last 12m; GPU OOM logs present (nvidia) on nodes i-0a1b2c*, queue length at batcher inlet at 65k items, avg batch size > configured max.

Alex M: I'm on it. From logs looks like continuous-batcher has a stuck batch aggregation loop; KV cache eviction also spiking. See sample from pod continuous-batcher-5: 
```
E0323 12:11:02.345 batcher.cpp:412] batch loop timed out, current_batch_size=0, waiting_for_aggregation=true
E0323 12:11:02.346 cuda: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
Stack: BatchManager::merge_batches -> KVCache::evict_if_needed -> cuda::alloc
```

Alex M: That cudaMalloc failure is causing the runtime to try to reallocate and ends up creating huge pending work that's never drained. Suspect deadlock between evict path and aggregation.

Dan (SRE): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) stop continuous batching for all traffic in us-east-1, 2) scale batcher replicas to 2 (down from 12) and set max_batch_size=1 to force synchronous handling, 3) route heavy customers to fallback CPU pool. I'll run commands unless someone objects.

Priya K: do it. Post the exact commands here.

Dan (SRE): running now:
```
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/continuous-batcher CONTINUOUS_BATCHING=false --context=cluster-us-east-1
kubectl -n inference scale deploy/continuous-batcher --replicas=2 --context=cluster-us-east-1
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/continuous-batcher MAX_BATCH_SIZE=1 --context=cluster-us-east-1
# apply fallback routing rule
redwood-router apply --cluster us-east-1 --route "model:prod->pool:fallback-cpu" --force
```

Priya K: executed first two. pods are restarting: continuous-batcher-5 -> Terminating, continuous-batcher-8 -> CrashLoopBackOff then restarted. Logs show a couple of nodes flapped at kubelet level (OOM kill). killing remainder of batcher pods to force cold start. :wrench:

EngRuntimeBot: Auto-scaler noticed drop, suspending auto-scale for batcher in us-east-1 for 15m to prevent oscillation.

Priya K: after restart latency dropped on a few routes — partial recovery. Need to confirm customer impact and who to notify.

Maya P: CS, which tenants are impacted? any paying Dedicated customers or just hosted?

Alex M: Looks like 3 dedicated tenants on reserved nodes in us-east-1 hit OOMs (acct-redwood-42, acct-bloom-7, acct-scribe). Several hosted API keys also saw 5xx for 5-12 minutes. I'm collecting per-tenant logs and will share.

CS Lead: Start triage emails to the three dedicated accounts and paste a short incident blurb in CS Slack. We need to offer a postmortem review. Prioritize acct-redwood-42 (highest SLO).

Priya K: Notifying account teams now. Draft to send: 
"We're investigating a high-priority incident impacting inference latency and errors in us-east-1 between 12:10 and 12:25 UTC. We have mitigations in place and are restoring traffic. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline."

(Reaction: :loudspeaker: from CS Lead)

Dan (SRE): Observability update: after disabling continuous batching and downscaling, 95p latency back to ~180ms, error rate to 0.6%. Queue length drained from 65k -> 4k in 8 minutes. GPU memory pressure reduced.

Alex M: I'm pushing a hotfix branch that short-circuits merge when KV cache reports high eviction pressure. PR: https://git.redwood/inference/continuous-batcher/pull/482 (WIP). The patch will avoid allocating during eviction and mark the batch for immediate flush.

Priya K: Can we canary the patch? If it looks good we'll roll to other regions.

Alex M: I'll land to canary (us-west-2) and run with continuous batching=true but with extra logging. Canaries scheduled in 10m.

EngRuntimeBot: fallback routing still active. Monitoring for 30m.

Dan (SRE): notes for post-incident: reproduce steps, heap/KV thresholds, add guardrails (max_pending_work), hard OOM circuit-breaker for continuous-batcher, add alert that triggers earlier on queue growth. Assign owners: Alex M (runtime fix), Dan (deploy guardrails), Priya (postmortem and customer comms).

Priya K: confirmed — I'll start postmortem doc and ping owners. Final status: mitigations applied, partial recovery, customer notifications in progress. Closing on-call handoff to next pager in 20m unless we see regression.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied at 12:18 UTC, partial restore confirmed at 12:26 UTC, monitoring.

Maya P: thanks team. Please include customer timeline and who we spoke to in the postmortem.

Priya K: will do.

(Conversation ends, follow-ups will continue in the postmortem doc.)
